claims.claim: Martin describes the Wild Cards non-mosaic volumes as stories threaded by an interstitial narrative he calls beads on a string.
claims.source: George R.R. Martin, interview reprinted at WildCardsWorld from SFFWorld
claims.quote: which we sometimes call the beads on a string

claims.claim: Publishers Weekly reports that the book's dramatic or salacious passages last only a few pages before returning to brisk summary.
claims.source: Publishers Weekly, review of Fire & Blood
claims.quote: they only last a few pages before a return to brisk summary

claims.claim: Chris Lough describes Fire & Blood as written in a dry, staid, objective tone unlike the Song of Ice and Fire novels.
claims.source: Chris Lough, review of Fire & Blood, Tor.com
claims.quote: featuring a dry, staid, objective tone

claims.claim: Martin insists Fire & Blood is not a novel but essentially a popular history, an entirely different literary form.
claims.source: George R.R. Martin, PW interview 'Imaginary History'

claims.claim: BookPage reports that Elio Garcia and Linda Antonsson read 10,000 pages of the novels to extract every reference to history, myth and legend.
claims.source: BookPage, 'George R.R. Martin: History is written in blood'
claims.quote: they pored over 10,000 pages of novels

claims.claim: The same reading reports a lexical density score between 4 and 4.5 for A Game of Thrones.
claims.source: A.R. Rivera, 'A Brief Linguistic Exam of A Song Of Ice And Fire'
claims.quote: A Game of Thrones has a score between 4 and 4.5
claims.page: section on lexical density and readability

claims.claim: The same reading gives A Game of Thrones an Automated Readability Index score of sixth grade.
claims.source: A.R. Rivera, 'A Brief Linguistic Exam of A Song Of Ice And Fire'
claims.quote: The ARI score for A Game of Thrones is sixth-grade
claims.page: section on lexical density and readability

claims.claim: A conference abstract announces a corpus of the first four ASOIAF novels rendered searchable in full for stylistic analysis.
claims.source: Matthew Voice (University of Sheffield), abstract 'Writing Westeros: a Corpus Linguistic Study', Nine Worlds Academia
claims.quote: the first four books of ASOIAF are rendered searchable in their entirety

claims.claim: Graham Oliver counts roughly twenty main characters and one source of tension introduced within the first five chapters of A Game of Thrones.
claims.source: Graham Oliver, 'How to Write Like George R. R. Martin', Fiction Advocate
claims.quote: a source of tension (Others) and 20 or so main characters

claims.claim: The same critic argues Martin pairs exposition with dramatic incident so that background arrives without stalling the reader.
claims.source: Graham Oliver, 'How to Write Like George R. R. Martin', Fiction Advocate
claims.quote: By pairing the exposition with the dramatic, you reduce the chances

claims.claim: Prosecraft's automated scan of A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms measures ly-adverbs at 0.46% of the text, which it places in the 3rd percentile of its library.
claims.source: Prosecraft (Shaxpir), book page for A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms, captured 2018

claims.claim: Prosecraft measures all adverbs in A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms at 2.26% of the text, which it places in the 9th percentile of its library.
claims.source: Prosecraft (Shaxpir), book page for A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms, captured 2018

claims.claim: Prosecraft measures non-ly adverbs in A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms at 1.80% of the text, which it places in the 34th percentile of its library, far higher than the same book's 3rd-percentile ly-adverb rank.
claims.source: Prosecraft (Shaxpir), book page for A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms, captured 2018

claims.claim: Prosecraft measures passive voice in A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms at 7.74% of the text, the 43rd percentile of its library.
claims.source: Prosecraft (Shaxpir), book page for A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms, captured 2018

claims.claim: Prosecraft states that its vividness model was trained by analysing hundreds of millions of words from thousands of different authors.
claims.source: Prosecraft (Shaxpir), book page for A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms, captured 2018
claims.quote: analyzed hundreds of millions of words, from thousands of different authors
